why: Both moved the same four chat sites with the same two real fixes and were equally honest about the three endpoints Router can't serve, but A's system-level work is broader and more rigorously measured — it found the silent untranslatable-param fallback that takes chat off Router entirely, built-measured-and-deleted the prompt cache key on a negative result, refused a vision fallback chain after watching grok hallucinate a user's image, and coordinated per-candidate Router timeouts against a client timeout it also discovered was 600s. B wins the single most important product trade — it measured latency per model and picked gpt-4o-mini (14.8x cheaper, same p50) over the cheap reasoning models A headlines, which is the right call for a typing-indicator chat — but it examined fewer Router levers, ran a third as much live traffic, and bundled a standard-tier pin that forfeits a measured 50% discount into the migration itself.
A_best: Evidence-driven restraint on the levers that looked attractive: the per-conversation cache key was built, measured as worthless (replayed history already caches), and deleted; the vision fallback chain was built and removed when the fallback confidently misdescribed a test image. Plus s2 — naming PRESENCE_PENALTY and N_CHOICES as settings that silently take the main path off Router, with traces.
B_best: It ranked the money items by latency as well as price, measuring p50 per candidate through the app's own request shape, and so rejected gpt-6-luna/claude-haiku (7.5s / 5.5s p50) for gpt-4o-mini (3.0s vs gpt-4o's 2.95s) — the correct reading of an interactive Telegram turn. The Flex-by-default account behaviour it caught is a genuine Router trap created by the move itself.
A_worst: Its top-ranked saving (gpt-6-luna, 24x) carries no latency measurement at all for a product where the user watches a typing indicator, and its Flex conclusion — 'nothing should be pinned to the standard tier' — rests on one sample being faster, which is not how an unbounded queue fails.
B_worst: Pinning service_tier default across the catalog it just unlocked throws away a measured 50% discount, and it ships that as part of the migration rather than as the operator decision it is; it also never flags which app settings make a request fall off Router silently, so an operator loses labels, cost and fallbacks without being told.
